contentBlocks.collectionInfo: The Northern Cape has the smallest population but the largest geographic area. Beneficiaries in remote towns like Upington and Springbok rely on mobile pay points and retailer cash collection — because distances are vast, direct bank transfer is strongly recommended here above all provinces.

contentBlocks.text: SASSA services in the Northern Cape

The Kimberley regional office coordinates the province's local offices and its extensive mobile network. Full-service offices handle applications, reviews and card services in the main population centres, while scheduled mobile units travel enormous distances each month to reach towns that have no permanent SASSA presence.
Grant collection in the Northern Cape

Distance shapes every collection decision in this province. The nearest full-service office to Upington is roughly four hours away in Kimberley, though Upington itself has retail pay points at Shoprite and Pick n Pay plus a monthly mobile unit visit.

For most beneficiaries outside Kimberley, the practical hierarchy is: bank transfer first (no travel at all), retailer Cash Send second (where chains operate), and scheduled mobile pay points as the fallback for towns with neither. If a mobile visit is missed, report it to the regional office and remember your balance waits for you.

items: Bank transfer eliminates travel across vast distances — switch free at any office.
Afrikaans-speaking staff are available at all branches.
Confirm mobile unit schedules before long trips; they shift monthly.

faqs.question: How do I get my grant in a remote town?
faqs.answer: Through scheduled mobile pay points or retailer collection where available. Direct bank transfer remains the strongest option to avoid long-distance travel entirely.

faqs.question: Where is the nearest SASSA office to Upington?
faqs.answer: The nearest full-service office is in Kimberley (roughly four hours' drive). Upington has retail pay points at Shoprite and Pick n Pay, and a mobile unit visits monthly.

faqs.question: Can I apply in Afrikaans?
faqs.answer: Yes. Afrikaans is widely spoken across the province and staff assist in Afrikaans at all branches.

faqs.question: What if the mobile pay point skips my town?
faqs.answer: Contact the Kimberley regional office on 053 802 7300 to report it. Your money stays available until collected — consider bank transfer to avoid future dependence on schedules.
